formats.note: Use the .ogg list where new Audio().canPlayType('audio/ogg; codecs="vorbis"') is not empty, else the parallel .mp3 list (Safari). Same order, same content.

loudness.note: Every file is peak-normalised to about -3 dBFS. 'gain' brings each cue to its category loudness target (max 100 ms K-weighted loudness, ITU-R BS.1770 filter); loops use integrated loudness.

userVolumes.note: Persist per player. 'effects' scales every bus except 'ambient'. Output = cue gain x bus level x effects (or ambient) x master.

voices.stealing: drop the new play if its priority is lower than every playing voice; otherwise stop the oldest voice with the lowest priority
voices.note: Per-cue caps are maxVoices; minIntervalMs drops repeats of the same cue that arrive sooner.

unlock: Browsers start an AudioContext suspended. Create it on load, call resume() inside the first pointerdown or keydown handler, and show the speaker icon as muted until then.

ui.hover.source: Freesound “Moving piece on a boardgame” by zachrau
ui.hover.author: zachrau
events: client: pointer enters a button, square or unit (throttle to 1 per 60 ms)
ui.hover.why: A fingertip tick of a wooden piece on the board, low-passed so it sits under everything; one tiny transient that never tires.

ui.click.author: mh2o
events: client: any button press without a more specific cue
ui.click.why: A stone piece set on an alabaster board: a dry, solid tock with no ring, the board-game equivalent of a button press.

ui.confirm.author: Kenney (www.kenney.nl)
events: client: an action is committed (move or target confirmed, confirmDeployment, dialog OK)
ui.confirm.why: A clay chip laid down firmly: a short, mid-heavy clack that says 'committed' without a musical tone.

ui.cancel.author: Kenney (www.kenney.nl)
events: client: action withdrawn, dialog cancelled, Escape or right-click
ui.cancel.why: A card slid back across felt: softer and lower-energy than confirm, so 'withdraw' is heard as the opposite gesture.

ui.error.source: rubberduck - 80 CC0 RPG SFX: lock_02.ogg + Kenney - Impact Sounds 1.0: Audio/impactWood_medium_002.ogg
ui.error.author: rubberduck (OpenGameArt); Kenney (www.kenney.nl)
events: a Rejection from validateIntent / submit for a player action (e.g. NOT_ENOUGH_AP, OUT_OF_RANGE)
ui.error.why: A locked latch that will not give plus a dull knock: the one UI sound with a rattle, so 'not allowed' is unmistakable.

ui.toggle.author: Kenney (www.kenney.nl)
events: client: a switch or segmented control (top / iso camera, settings)
ui.toggle.why: A real mechanical switch, short and mid-pitched; distinct from click (stone) and confirm (clay).

ui.open.author: Joseph SARDIN
events: client: a panel or dialog opens (unit card, army builder, log)
ui.open.why: A campaign map unfolded on the table: papery, brief, and in keeping with the parchment UI skin.

ui.close.author: Joseph SARDIN
events: client: a panel or dialog closes
ui.close.why: A book shut on the table: a short, soft thump that closes the gesture ui.open started.

lobby.joined.author: GlaneurDeSons
events: session: the opponent joins the lobby (netcode layer, not an engine event)
lobby.joined.why: A small hand bell like a shop door bell: someone has walked in.

lobby.ready.author: DavidGreck
events: readyChanged (ready: true), either seat
lobby.ready.why: A coin dropped into a cup: your stake is in. Keeps the coin motif from the first screen.

turn.start.own.author: Pierre SIBANARCO
events: turnStarted (seat = me)
turn.start.own.why: One warm bronze bell strike: bright, short and pleasant, the only 'go' signal that is tonal.

turn.start.opponent.author: Joseph SARDIN
events: turnStarted (seat = opponent)
turn.start.opponent.why: A single low war-drum boom pitched down: ominous and clearly not your bell.

turn.end.source: rubberduck - 100 CC0 metal and wood SFX: wood_hit_07.ogg
turn.end.author: rubberduck (OpenGameArt)
events: turnEnded (seat = me), or the endTurn intent accepted
turn.end.why: Two knuckle knocks on the table, the gesture players use to pass.

timer.warning.source: BigSoundBank “Tic Tac Mechanical Alarm Clock #3 (#2656)” by Joseph SARDIN
timer.warning.author: Joseph SARDIN
events: client turn timer (R29): once per second in the last 10 s of the turn time and again in the last 10 s of the bank
timer.warning.why: One tick-tock of a mechanical clock; play once per second in the last 10 s, never as a loop.

boost.active.author: Joseph SARDIN
events: approach boost (R28): the first turnStarted of the battle while AP is doubled, and once more when the view's firstContactRound becomes set (the boost ends with that round)
boost.active.why: One real horn call at first contact: a battlefield signal everyone understands; used once per match.

unit.select.source: BigSoundBank “Coin spinning on a table #4 (#2700)” by Pierre SIBANARCO + BigSoundBank “Coin spinning on a table #5 (#2701)” by Pierre SIBANARCO
unit.select.author: Pierre SIBANARCO
events: client: an own unit is selected
unit.select.why: A two-euro coin tapped on a wooden table (same recording session as the death sounds), nudged up a semitone: picking up your piece.

unit.deselect.source: BigSoundBank “Coin spinning on a table #2 (#2698)” by Pierre SIBANARCO
unit.deselect.author: Pierre SIBANARCO
events: client: selection cleared

unit.deselect.why: The same coin set back down, two semitones lower and quieter: the inverse of select.

unit.move.step.source: Freesound “coin sliding on table.wav” by seanhealey
unit.move.step.author: seanhealey
events: unitMoved (one event per step): space the plays 120-160 ms apart to match the token animation
unit.move.step.why: One short slide of a large coin across a wooden table per square: metal-on-wood grit, under 0.4 s so steps stay countable.

unit.move.charge.source: Freesound “coin sliding on table.wav” by seanhealey + BigSoundBank “Whoosh #8 (#1801)” by Joseph SARDIN
unit.move.charge.author: seanhealey; Joseph SARDIN
events: the first unitMoved of a charge intent (R26); its other steps use unit.move.step at -3 dB
unit.move.charge.why: A longer coin slide with a metal-tube whoosh on top: the move and the intent to strike in one gesture.

march.step.source: Freesound “several coins on wood top” by nicoproson
march.step.author: nicoproson
events: the unitMoved events of one groupMarch intent (R27): one play per march wave, not one per unit
march.step.why: Several coins rattling across wood at once: a group step that is obviously plural; one sound per march, not per unit.

events: defendChanged (defending: true, reason: action)
unit.defend.why: A heavy weight planted on a wooden floor with a faint plate ring: bracing behind a shield, low and short.

events: unitAttacked, melee, attacker Power below 10
attack.swing.light.why: Short real combat whooshes (Zoom H6 recordings), high-passed: fast air, no metal, so the hit that follows carries the material.

attack.swing.heavy.author: Joseph SARDIN
events: unitAttacked, melee, attacker Power 10 or more, or a Size-2 attacker
attack.swing.heavy.why: Longer whooshes of a bamboo stick, a long wooden stick and a metal tube, two semitones down: weight you can hear before the blow lands.
